def: One attempt by an agent at a task; agent evals run several trials per task because outputs vary.
The final state of the environment when a trial ends, such as whether a refund exists in the database.
The complete record of a trial: messages, tool calls, results and reasoning, also called a trace or trajectory.
Scoring an agent by comparing the final state of the world with a goal state or invariants, instead of judging its words or its route.
A model or script that plays the customer in an agent evaluation, following a hidden instruction and replying to the agent.
A benchmark that grades agents in simulated customer conversations by the database state they leave and reports reliability as pass^k.
The chance that at least one of k attempts at a task succeeds, a measure of capability that rises with k.
The chance that all k attempts at a task succeed, a measure of reliability that falls as k grows.
The code around a model that lets it act as an agent: prompts, tools, loop and limits, evaluated together with the model.
Cheap automatic measures of a run, such as steps, tool errors, repeated calls and cap hits, used to find trials worth reading.
Total spend on all trials divided by the number of successful trials, which exceeds cost per attempt because failures also cost money.
